implementation_notes: The ecosystem realization is tower: the target is a Service, and a filter is a Layer whose layer() method wraps that service in a new service that does its work before and after call(). axum applies layers with .layer(...) on a Router, and axum::middleware::from_fn builds the same layer from an async fn(Request, Next) -> Response, which is the idiomatic shape for one-off filters; tower-http supplies the common ones (TraceLayer, CompressionLayer, CorsLayer). Hand-writing a Vec<Box<dyn Service>> chain is unnecessary in an axum or tonic stack; it remains the fallback when the transport is not tower-based.
pitfalls: Router::layer wraps only the routes registered before it, so a route added afterwards is silently unfiltered (use route_layer or register layers last).
A hand-written Layer must forward Service::poll_ready to the inner service; ignoring it breaks back-pressure and load-shedding layers.
Holding a Mutex or RefCell borrow across an await inside a layer blocks the runtime or panics - shared filter state needs Arc<Mutex<..>> with the lock scoped to synchronous code.
